# Official overtime result fixtures

Retrieved 2026-11-03 from primary sources. `officialResults.json` contains factual scores, period totals,
ordered goals where available, and a source URL for every match. No article bodies, player images or live
network calls are included. These are independent sporting outcomes, not expected values generated by the reducer.

## Collections and selection

- NBA: Knicks–Hawks 2017 (4 OT), Nuggets–Trail Blazers 2019 playoffs (4 OT), Kings–Clippers 2023 (2 OT).
  Period scores come from `props.pageProps.game.awayTeam.periods` / `homeTeam.periods` in each official
  nba.com game's `__NEXT_DATA__`; final scores are the separate published `score` fields.
- NHL: every Florida Panthers overtime playoff game in 2023 (seven games), plus the first three OT and first
  two shootout games in their 2022–23 regular-season schedule. Selection source:
  <https://api-web.nhle.com/v1/club-schedule-season/FLA/20222023>. Each game's official `landing` JSON supplies
  period descriptors, ordered goals, overall score and last-period type. Only approved goals are counted;
  the overturned first-overtime goal in Carolina–Florida game 1 is not a scoring event.
- Historical NHL: the first two Florida ties in the 1996–97 schedule, selected from
  <https://api-web.nhle.com/v1/club-schedule-season/FLA/19961997>. These prove finite overtime ending level.
- Football: Belgium–USA 2014 and Portugal–France 2016 (exactly two extra halves); France–Italy 2000
  (golden goal); Greece–Czech Republic 2004 (silver goal); France–Switzerland 2021 (still tied after extra time,
  then penalties). RBFA, UEFA and FFF reports are linked per fixture. Historical golden/silver rules are
  supported by those historical reports, not inferred from today's IFAB rules.

## Rule mapping

| Competition/rule                                                      | Format used for covered scoring |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------- |
| NBA, 12-minute quarters / repeated 5-minute OT                        | `QTR4XA-S:T12P-O:U/T5P`         |
| NHL playoffs, repeated 20-minute sudden-death periods                 | `PER3XA-S:T20P-O:USD/T20P`      |
| NHL regular season / historical tie, one 5-minute sudden-death period | `PER3XA-S:T20P-O:1SD/T5P`       |
| Football, mandatory two 15-minute extra halves                        | `HAL2XA-S:T45P-O:2X/T15P`       |
| Historical football golden goal                                       | `HAL2XA-S:T45P-O:2SD/T15P`      |
| Historical football silver goal                                       | `HAL2XA-S:T45P-O:2/T15P`        |

NBA timing/repetition: <https://official.nba.com/rule-no-5-scoring-and-timing/>, sections II and IV.
NHL contemporary rules: <https://media.nhl.com/site/asset/public/ext/2022-23/2022-23Rulebook.pdf>, rule 84.
Historical NHL rule changes: <https://records.nhl.com/history/historical-rule-changes> (1983–84 and 2005–06).
Modern football extra time: <https://www.theifab.com/laws/latest/determining-the-outcome-of-a-match/>.

## Interpretation and coverage limits

NBA/NHL sides are away, home; football uses the named fixture order. Periods contain period scores, not
cumulative scores. Zero-goal periods are retained. Football stoppage time belongs to its explicitly identified
period: a 90+ goal is not silently classified as overtime, nor is a 105+1 silver goal put into the second extra half.
UEFA and FFF differ on Delvecchio's regulation goal minute in the EURO 2000 final; the fixture records its
uncontested second-half placement rather than choosing one minute. Trezeguet's golden goal is at 103 minutes.

`scope: throughOvertime` marks three shootout cases: two NHL games and France–Switzerland. Tests assert the
drawn sporting score through overtime, not the eventual shootout winner. NHL adds a shootout winner's goal to
its published final score; it is excluded from `playedScore`. Football penalties remain a separate score.
No real shootout is relabeled as `F:TB1`, and these cases do not establish full shootout support.

Tests replay period totals and actual ordered goals for hockey/football. NBA point replay uses a deliberately
synthetic order from the published period totals, not historical play-by-play; it checks input-level parity and
that an ordinary overtime lead does not end the period. Period-end events are supplied explicitly, as the
existing scoring engine requires; fixtures do not claim autonomous clock-expiry enforcement.
All tests use the internal overtime opt-in; public activation remains gated for the later record/view slice.
